text:
alexm: FYI — saw a spike this morning where a few tenants with lots of short streaming calls ate ~40% of the metering throughput for ~10m. Billing shows a big skew. we need a plan for fair accounting + correct attribution for partial/streamed tokens. anyone seen this pattern before?

priya: ugh, yeah. streaming partial tokens are always messy. do we currently attribute per-chunk or wait until final chunk?

alexm: right now we attribute on finalization which means if clients disconnect mid-stream we lose the prompt-side tokens or they go into a fuzzy bucket. that causes both underbilling and audit gaps.

lucy: quick idea: incrementally emit provisional events per chunk with a flag "provisional":true and a later finalize event that sets provisional:false + ties to the trace id. then reconciler coalesces. cheaper for tail-heavy workloads and gives observability.

omar: that model sounds ok but watch out for double-counting if both provisional and final remain. reconciler must be idempotent and use event_id or sequence numbers. also need a TTL for hanging provisional events.

priya: agreed. proposal: per-tenant leaky-bucket at ingress to cap burst consumption (soft limit) + a priority queue that favors steady tenants. provide per-route token guarantees for higher tiers.

alexm: +1. we should also emit a minimal provisional schema so downstream billing can start showing near-real-time usage without committing invoices. example schema: 

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_123",
  "tenant_id": "tn_789",
  "kind": "token_usage",
  "provisional": true,
  "tokens": {"prompt": 123, "completion": 45},
  "seq": 12,
  "trace_id": "trace-abc"
}
```

lucy: nice. we then need a reconciliation flow that consumes final events and emits corrections as negative events or adjustments. important: downstream must accept adjustments as first-class (not just heuristics).

omar: what about late arrivals? if final comes hours later, do we accept and invoice? finance will hate surprises. maybe have a cut window for invoiceable events and treat anything after that as adjustments on next billing cycle.

finance-bot: tagging @finance — we need SLA on max lag for invoiceable usage. recommended: 24h cut for reported usage, anything after goes as an adjustment with clear flag. also require ability to filter adjustments per invoice.

priya: +1 on 24h cut. but for enterprise tenants on contracts we might allow longer tails with delayed invoices. need config per account.

alexm: ops question — how to store provisional events cheaply? we could keep them in a compact append-only store keyed by (tenant, trace) and GC on finalize or TTL. avoid full enrichment until finalize to save cost.

lucy: yep. enrichment can be deferred: store raw provisional, enrich on finalization or in bulk for reconciliation. that also means our observability dashboards need to show provisional vs finalized counts.

omar: another tradeoff: sampling. for ultra-high-volume tenants, emit 1/n provisional events and scale counts. must carry a sampling factor in the schema so reconciler can upweight. sampler helps keep ingestion and audit costs bounded.

alexm: agree. include fields: sample_rate, sampled=true/false. reconciler must honor sample_rate when combining. keep sampling deterministic per-session to avoid oscillation.

lucy: ops note: we need a backpressure signal to callers when tenant hits soft limit. simple 429 with Retry-After may be ok for public API. for dedicated capacity customers maybe queue with delayed ack.

priya: and we should add an internal metric: "provisional_retention" and "late_final_rate" so we can alert on growing deltas between provisional and finalized tokens.

alexm: next steps I propose: 1) spec provisional/final event schema + sampling fields, 2) add per-tenant ingress leaky-bucket + tiered queueing, 3) reconciler rule doc (idempotency keys, negative adjustments, invoice cut window), 4) dashboards and alerts. I'll open an RFC doc.

omar: sg, I'll sketch reconciler semantics (idempotent apply, negative adjustments accepted, sample upweighting) and drop a small prototype.

lucy: I'll own UI flags (provisional vs finalized) and dashboards + a small alert playbook.

priya: I'll wire ingress rate limiter and queue policy config in the load-shed controller. will post PR with config knobs.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: metering-provisional-schema -> staging at 2023-11-15T02:30:00Z :rocket:

alexm: thanks all. tagging the doc here: https://redwood.internal/docs/metering-provisional-reconcile (draft). please add review comments in the RFC. :thumbsup:

finance-bot: noted. will add billing impact checklist to RFC.

alexm: cool — will ping when RFC ready for review.
